answer.rationale: The two measured declines this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing the funnel entrance is the intervention most likely to compound into durable qualified revenue rather than a one-quarter bump. Two independent inherited records point the same way (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on signup-field reduction), which makes this the best-corroborated direction; memory_91 (activation messaging) would treat a symptom further downstream and can follow if onboarding alone does not recover activation. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing even though it is the most direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 is the most decision-relevant and also the most overclaimed record in the set (acquisition lift, revenue lift, time-to-first-value, and generalization across both billing plans, all from a single day-31 consolidation), and discount-acquired price-sensitive SMB cohorts are exactly where headline acquisition gains tend to mask retention and margin erosion. Matching a competitor on price also risks resetting willingness-to-pay for the segment permanently, which cuts against the sustainable long-term objective. So I spend verification on memory_73 (to see whether the revenue lift was ever measured past the promotional window, and whether 'qualified' revenue was the metric) and on memory_86 (to confirm the onboarding lift was a real completion/time-to-value gain and not a definitional artifact of removing steps, and that it held beyond week one). If memory_73's source record turns out to show durable post-promotion retention, pricing becomes a live option next slot; if memory_86 collapses under inspection, I fall back to activation_messaging on memory_91. Referral incentive (memory_57) is set aside because it acts on established customers and does nothing for the two metrics currently declining, and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the source of this quarter's loss. Standard experiment scale with a churn-and-margin guardrail on the acquired cohort, not a broad rollout, since both supporting memories are consolidated summaries whose underlying effect sizes I have not yet seen.
